gen-dafont-klaudia-fs-supreme: Loose, inky handwriting with a luxe wink. Supreme runs beneath it as a dense, sturdy sans, its letters held open, so a long paragraph feels steady and crisp.
gen-dafont-klaudia-satoshi: Satoshi stands tall and friendly, its wide e never pinching shut and every stroke cut to one width. Klaudia is the one for flowing, pen-written flourish; Satoshi simply keeps going.
gen-dafont-klaudia-switzer: Switzer reads tidy and tubular, with a tall waist line. Give it a bit more size than the script above and its c tips stay clearly apart, while Klaudia's pen-written flow adds a casual, luxurious touch.
gen-dafont-klaudia-work-sans: Work Sans reads modern and sturdy, with a high mean line and c tips held clearly apart. Klaudia does the flowing, pen-written flourish, while Work Sans does the quiet, dependable carrying of the text.
gen-dafont-klill-fs-hind: Hind is a sturdy sans-serif whose lowercase nearly matches its capitals, with strokes like drawn string. Hind and Klill look so alike in build that their shared trait is simply steadiness, with curve endings never closing in.
gen-dafont-lemon-milk-gf-cascadia-mono: Lemon Milk spreads its rounded letters wide, loose and friendly, like a rolling-ball pen trail. And Cascadia Mono answers with compact plain sans letters that stand like pins, capitals blending into lowercase.
gen-dafont-lemon-milk-gf-julius-sans-one: Wide-open, whisper-light lettering with a bright, rounded grin up top. Julius Sans One follows with big gaps between letters and curves left open at the ends, so a long page feels spacious and unhurried.
gen-dafont-lemon-milk-gf-lexend-exa: Lexend Exa has a big x-height, stubby ascenders and wide curves that stay distinct. Lexend Exa carries a long page smoothly, while Lemon Milk's loose, rounded heading sets a friendly, striking tone.
gen-dafont-lemon-milk-gf-lexend-giga: Lexend Giga draws flat, single-weight lines with generous tracking that opens up every word. Lexend Giga makes a long page feel unhurried, while Lemon Milk's rounded heading letters add a friendly, striking spread.
gen-dafont-lemon-milk-gf-lexend-mega: Lexend Mega looks drawn with one nib, its body height nearly matching the capitals and each c showing a visible gap. And Lemon Milk's loose, rounded heading leads into text that stays approachable paragraph after paragraph.
